confidence.rationale: Recent review supports the phenomenon while identifying multiple encoding and retrieval accounts.

scope.population: Humans studied with laboratory memory paradigms.
scope.temporal_scope: Within or across experimental learning episodes.

claims.statement: Proactive interference is impaired memory for newer information associated with previously learned information; it is not a unique mechanism label.

confidence.rationale: Reviews support retrieval competition as one account but also identify encoding contributions and task dependence.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The account is weakened where interference remains after retrieval competition is eliminated and is fully explained by encoding-stage differences.

boundary_conditions: Does not assert that all proactive-interference effects arise at retrieval.
scope.population: Humans in successive memory tasks with competing material.

claims.statement: Activated prior traces can reduce current target retrieval through competition at retrieval.
claims.temporal_ordering: Prior traces are activated before or during the current retrieval attempt.

confidence.rationale: The computational term is well defined, although neural interpretations remain model-dependent.

claims.statement: Reward prediction error is a model-defined discrepancy term used to update expected value.

confidence.rationale: Strong as a formal model relation, but correspondence with a unique biological process is not assumed.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The hypothesis fails for a dataset if a preregistered temporal-difference model cannot predict held-out choice updates better than specified alternatives.

boundary_conditions: Applies only when the specified model provides an adequate account of choices.
scope.population: Agents or organisms modeled with temporal-difference reinforcement learning.

claims.statement: A reward prediction-error term changes later action-value estimates under a temporal-difference update rule.
claims.temporal_ordering: Outcome and prediction error on trial t precede the updated value used on a later trial.

confidence.rationale: Physiological review supports multiple feedback sites and receptor contributions rather than one simple loop.

claims.statement: Glucocorticoid negative feedback comprises receptor-linked processes that regulate subsequent HPA activity and contribute to pulsatile dynamics.

confidence.rationale: Broad mechanism is established physiologically, but this generic PMM record does not identify site, receptor, timing, or estimand.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: A scoped version is challenged if selective interruption of the specified receptor pathway leaves the preregistered downstream HPA response unchanged.

boundary_conditions: Receptor subtype, tissue, timing, and basal versus stress regime must be specified in empirical claims.

claims.statement: Increases in glucocorticoid signaling contribute to limiting or reshaping later HPA secretory drive.
claims.temporal_ordering: Glucocorticoid signaling precedes the regulated later secretory activity.

confidence.rationale: The term is operationally useful when partner, modality, stressor, and outcome are specified.

scope.population: Children exposed to a controlled social-evaluative stress task.

claims.statement: Social buffering denotes a change in stress-response magnitude or trajectory attributable to a social condition.

confidence.rationale: The randomized trial reported a condition-by-trial interaction, but the effect estimate was not extracted beyond p < .05.

interaction_term.notes: Reported p < .05; parent condition differed from alone and researcher conditions in post-hoc tests.

limitations: A statistical interaction is not itself an identified mediating mechanism.

boundary_conditions: Does not generalize automatically to adults, other support partners, or subjective stress.
scope.population: 180 children aged 11-15 years in the MISTiC experiment.

claims.statement: Randomized social-buffer condition modified the post-stressor cortisol trajectory across sampling trials.

causal_assumptions.consistency: Each randomized condition corresponds to the protocol-defined interaction.
causal_assumptions.exchangeability: Supported by random assignment; implementation details were not independently audited here.
causal_assumptions.interference: Assumed no effect of one child's assignment on another child's cortisol response.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Three conditions were assigned in the trial.

claims.causal_estimand: Intention-to-treat contrast in repeated cortisol trajectory for parent buffer versus randomized comparison conditions.

confidence.rationale: Random assignment supports a causal condition contrast, while the extracted record lacks a numerical standardized effect.

limitations: Numerical effect size and allocation details require full-text extraction before expert review.

boundary_conditions: Estimand is assignment to the study condition, not social support in all settings.
scope.population: 180 children aged 11-15 years in the MISTiC experiment.

claims.statement: Assignment to the parent-buffer condition changed the cortisol stress-response trajectory relative to comparison conditions.
claims.temporal_ordering: Buffer assignment and interactions preceded post-stressor cortisol measurements.

evidence.design: Critical review of behavioral and imaging studies across proactive-interference paradigms.

evidence.design: Perspective integrating computational accounts and dopamine findings.

evidence.summary: Multiple receptor-linked negative-feedback processes contribute to glucocorticoid pulsatility and HPA regulation.

objects.definition: Experimental context in which currently relevant material is tested after earlier, potentially competing material has been encoded.
objects.label: Successive memory-task context
objects.scope: Human laboratory memory tasks; exact interference depends on task and material similarity.

objects.definition: Experimental or computational context with states, actions, outcomes, and trial-wise value updating.
objects.label: Reinforcement-learning task context
objects.scope: Model-based description; neural implementation requires separate claims.

objects.definition: Physiological context covering basal or stress-related hypothalamic- pituitary-adrenal activity and glucocorticoid feedback.
objects.label: HPA-axis regulatory context
objects.scope: Mammalian physiology; timing and receptor contributions vary by regime and tissue.

objects.definition: Controlled stress context involving social evaluation and repeated physiological sampling after the stressor.
objects.label: Social-evaluative stress context
objects.scope: The pilot result below is restricted to children aged 11-15 years.

boundary_notes: This label denotes a performance phenomenon, not one uniquely established mechanism.
Encoding competition and retrieval competition must remain distinguishable hypotheses.
objects.definition: Impairment of memory for newer target information associated with prior learning or activation of competing information.
objects.label: Proactive interference

objects.definition: Previously encoded information that remains available and can compete with current targets.
objects.label: Activated prior memory traces

objects.definition: Observable response reporting the currently relevant target item.
objects.label: Target recall response
objects.response_topography: Spoken, typed, or selected target response.

objects.definition: Accuracy or latency of retrieval for currently relevant target information.
objects.label: Target retrieval performance

objects.definition: Proposed process in which activated prior traces compete with a current target during retrieval, reducing target accessibility or selection.
objects.label: Retrieval competition from prior traces
realization_conditions: Prior and current information are both available at retrieval.
The task creates competition through overlap, recency, or response conflict.

objects.definition: Difference in target accuracy or latency between interference and matched control conditions.
objects.label: Proactive-interference cost
objects.method: Contrast performance after competing prior material with an appropriate noncompeting baseline.

boundary_notes: A computational variable is not identical to a dopamine signal.
Distributional, sensory, and belief-state variants require explicit model specifications.
objects.definition: Computational discrepancy between received and expected reward, commonly extended in temporal-difference models to include discounted next-state value.
objects.label: Reward prediction error

objects.definition: Current model-derived estimate of expected future return for an action in a state.
objects.label: Expected action value

objects.definition: Appetitive consequence delivered or observed on a learning trial.
objects.label: Received reward

objects.definition: Computational process that changes a value estimate as a function of a prediction-error term and a learning-rate parameter.
objects.label: Temporal-difference value updating
realization_conditions: A formally specified update rule links trial outcomes to later value estimates.
Learning rate and state representation are identified or estimated.

objects.definition: Trial-wise latent prediction-error estimate generated by a fitted reinforcement-learning model.
objects.label: Fitted trial-wise reward prediction error
objects.method: Fit a preregistered learning model to choices and outcomes, then compute trial-wise latent values.

objects.definition: Time-indexed concentration of cortisol or corticosterone in circulation.
objects.label: Circulating glucocorticoid level

objects.definition: Time-indexed activity promoting downstream glucocorticoid secretion within the HPA axis.
objects.label: HPA secretory drive

objects.definition: Physiological feedback process through which glucocorticoid signaling contributes to limiting or shaping subsequent HPA-axis secretory activity.
objects.label: Glucocorticoid negative feedback on HPA activity
realization_conditions: Glucocorticoid and/or mineralocorticoid receptor signaling is available.
Temporal regime and tissue location are specified.

objects.definition: Experimental pharmacological manipulation used to probe glucocorticoid feedback sensitivity.
objects.delivery: Timed administration followed by endocrine sampling under a specified protocol.
objects.label: Dexamethasone challenge

objects.definition: Repeated cortisol assay used to characterize level, trajectory, or pulsatility over time.
objects.label: Serial cortisol measurement
objects.method: Repeated saliva, plasma, or other validated matrix sampling with time stamps.

objects.definition: Controlled task manipulation intended to elicit a social-evaluative stress response.
objects.label: Standardized psychosocial stressor

objects.definition: Randomized condition providing brief parent interaction around a social-evaluative stressor.
objects.delivery: Brief audiovisual parent interaction at protocol-defined time points.
objects.label: Parent social-buffer condition

objects.definition: Ordered sequence of post-stressor sampling occasions used to estimate response trajectory.
objects.label: Post-stressor sampling time course

objects.definition: Time-indexed change in cortisol concentration following a defined stressor.
objects.label: Cortisol stress-response trajectory

boundary_notes: An observed buffering effect does not by itself identify the mediating mechanism.
objects.definition: Family of processes through which a social partner or social signal changes the magnitude or time course of a stress response.
objects.label: Social buffering of physiological stress

objects.method: Baseline and repeated post-stressor salivary cortisol assays.
